text:
Venezuela Spot Oil Sales Snarled by Surging Freight Costs
•Sales of Venezuelan oil for loading in October stalled after a surge in shipping costs muddled negotiations between the country’s state oil company and buyers of its oil.
•Shipping costs have more than doubled from the end of August, making Venezuelan crude less competitive with Canadian barrels for US refiners and snarling sales deals.
•The dispute risks disrupting a key source of crude for American refiners amid record diesel prices and ahead of US midterm elections.
By Lucia Kassai
(Bloomberg) -- Sales of Venezuelan oil for loading in October stalled after a surge in shipping costs muddled negotiations between the country’s state oil company and buyers of its oil.
Shipping costs — a key component of the delivered price — have more than doubled from the end of August. That’s making Venezuelan crude less competitive with Canadian barrels for US refiners and snarling sales deals, according to people with knowledge of the situation. Canada and Venezuela are the largest suppliers of foreign oil to the US.
Commodity traders such as Vitol Group and Trafigura Group, tapped by the US to help sell Venezuelan oil, have a broad arrangement — but not an obligation — to buy oil from Petroleos de Venezuela SA. Buyers of Venezuelan oil are currently being offered the oil at a discount of around $14 to benchmark ICE Brent prices, loading in October, said the people, who asked not to be named discussing private information.
With the cost to ship oil to the US Gulf Coast at nearly $7 a barrel, it means the oil arrives at the shores of Texas and Louisiana at a discount of $7 per barrel, or at least $5 more expensive than competing Canadian supplies, the people said.

Texas authorites booked Mohammed Rahhal as “White” on an immigration hold and a $15,000 drug bond.

Grand Prairie police arrested the 43-year-old on Aug. 31, 2026. The inmate file lists a felony drug count for 1 to 4 grams.

Nearly a month later, no public Grand Prairie or ICE release names his country of origin or says whether he was transferred, deported, or cut loose.

Federal Statistical Policy Directive 15, in the 1997 version still used by many jails, folded Middle Eastern and North African origins into the ‘White’ racial category.

OMB added a separate Middle Eastern or North African category in March 2024. Agencies have until March 28, 2029, to finish the switch.

The Dallas Express documented the same coding on an Afghan national booked in Tarrant County after a Fort Worth bomb-threat case. That jail search offered white, black, Asian, or Indian.

Gov. Greg Abbott's office has not posted a disposition on this hold. Grand Prairie Police have not posted a follow-up naming an ICE pickup.

text:
Daily Morning Market Brief
Date: 24/09/2026

Global markets have come under pressure as the deadly combination of rising crude oil prices and US bond yields has resurfaced. Brent crude moved above $102 as uncertainty over a possible Strait of Hormuz blockade intensified, while hopes of near-term peace talks remained stalled on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly. Additional supply-side concerns emerged over potential US restrictions on diesel exports, further supporting oil prices.

US bond yields also moved higher after stronger-than-expected manufacturing and services PMI data increased expectations of further rate hikes. Fed Governor Michael Barr’s comments that additional rate hikes may be required to bring inflation under control, along with weak demand at a US bond auction, added to the upward pressure on yields.

Overnight, US markets declined, with all major indices under pressure. The Nasdaq fell 1.13% to close at 26,936.04, while broader US indices declined by more than 0.50%. European markets also ended lower. US futures are currently showing a subdued trend, while Asian markets are trading mixed. Japan’s Nikkei, reopening after a three-day holiday, is up nearly 1.50%, while the Hang Seng is down around 0.50%. South Korea’s KOSPI remains closed on account of Thanksgiving.

The extension of the US-China trade truce under the Busan agreement until January 10, 2027, provides additional time for both sides to work towards a broader economic deal and remains one of the few positive developments amid the current global weakness.

Domestic News Flow

NSE will make its market debut today after raising ₹22,562 crore through its IPO, with the listing taking place on the BSE.

Insurance stocks will remain in focus after IRDAI proposed a broad overhaul of the economics of insurance distribution. The consultation paper seeks lower Expense of Management (EoM) limits, tighter controls on commissions and greater transparency for policyholders.

BDL has signed an ₹810.79 crore contract with the Ministry of Defence for the supply of Satellite Smart Anti-Airfield Weapons (SAT-SAAW), along with associated equipment, to the Indian Air Force.

Exide Industries’ subsidiary, Exide Energy Solutions (EESL), has completed the commissioning of Phase-I of its 6 GWh lithium-ion cell manufacturing facility at Devanahalli, Bengaluru.

Telecom stocks will also remain in focus after TRAI directed service providers to offer voice-and-SMS-only tariff plans, without bundled data, with a minimum validity of 30 days or less.

Market Strategy

Indian markets are expected to open with a sharp gap down following the weak global cues. However, traders should avoid rushing into fresh short positions at the open and instead wait for a decent pullback or a failed recovery before considering shorts.

The BSE indices’ monthly expiry could further increase volatility and intraday choppiness. Traders should therefore remain cautious and account for sharp swings before taking fresh positions.

Overall strategy: Wait for a pullback before entering shorts rather than chasing the gap-down opening.

text:
The Legend of Mossy Hollow
In the low country of Louisiana, where the cypress knees rise from black water like the fingers of drowned men and Spanish moss hangs in gray curtains, there once stood a drowsy settlement called Mossy Hollow. The people there were a mixture of planters, poor whites, freedmen, and those who still worked the cane and cotton for little more than rations. Superstition ran thicker than the humidity. Everyone knew the old stories of conjure and the restless dead.

Into this place came Ichabod Crane, a lanky schoolmaster from up North with a long neck, a hungry look, and an appetite that could empty a pot of gumbo before the first bowl was offered to anyone else. He boarded with the Widow LaFleur and taught the children their letters in a one-room schoolhouse that smelled of mildew and woodsmoke. Ichabod had a particular weakness for rich food, pretty girls, and the prospect of marrying into property.The prettiest girl and the richest prize was Miss Delphine Beaumont, daughter of a planter whose land still produced after the war. Delphine had dark eyes, a laugh like wind in the cane, and suitors enough to fill a gallery. Foremost among them was Brom “Bones” Thibodaux, a broad-shouldered local who raced horses, drank, and played rough jokes. Brom did not take kindly to the Yankee schoolteacher hovering around Delphine.

One autumn evening, after a supper of fried catfish, cornbread, and sweet potato pie at the Beaumont place, the talk turned, as it always did in Mossy Hollow, to the thing that haunted the old river road.
They called him Papa Cane.

Long ago, before the war ended, a cruel overseer named Cane had been slighted by a newly freed man who refused to bow or step aside on the path. The overseer swore he would see that man and all like him brought low. He died badly—fever, some said, or a curse laid by a root worker—and was buried without ceremony. Not long after, a houngan from the back swamp raised him as a zombie, bound to the earth and to his old hatred. Papa Cane shambled the night roads with milky eyes and rotting clothes, and he carried, of all things, watermelons. He hurled them with terrible force at those he took for “poor black folk” still walking free. The fruit would burst against trees, wagons, or skulls, leaving red pulp and seeds like scattered teeth. Travelers swore they heard the wet thud and the zombie’s low, wordless moan of old grievance.Ichabod laughed a little too loudly at the tale, but when he rode home that night on a borrowed plow horse, the laughter died. The road wound through the cypress swamp. Moonlight silvered the water. Then he heard it: a heavy, dragging step, and the sound of something large being hefted.Papa Cane came out of the mist. The zombie’s head lolled, jaw slack, but his arms were strong. He lifted a watermelon the size of a child’s torso and flung it. It smashed against a cypress trunk beside Ichabod’s horse, spraying juice and black seeds. The schoolmaster kicked the horse into a gallop. Another melon whistled past his ear. A third struck the horse’s flank and burst. Ichabod clung to the saddle, coat flapping, as the zombie pursued with unnatural speed, still hurling fruit and still nursing that ancient slight.

At the old wooden bridge over the bayou, Ichabod looked back. Papa Cane stood in the middle of the road, another melon raised. Ichabod felt something strike the back of his head—wet, heavy, final. He tumbled from the horse.The next morning the horse wandered home alone. Of Ichabod Crane there was no sign except his hat, lying in the mud, and the smashed remains of several watermelons, seeds glistening in the sun. Some said he had been carried off by the zombie. Others whispered that Brom Thibodaux knew more than he told, and that a certain large, laughing man had been seen that same night with a wagonload of melons.Delphine married Brom before the year was out. On quiet nights in Mossy Hollow, when the moss sways and the frogs go silent, folks still claim you can hear the wet impact of fruit against wood, and the dragging step of a dead man who never forgot a slight.

KEY JUDGMENT

We assess Washington is attempting to compress Havana’s strategic options through escalating economic, financial, energy, and diplomatic pressure while preserving channels for negotiated concessions.

Intent: reduce liquidity and increase competition for resources within the Cuban state.

16 OCTOBER–30 NOVEMBER 2026

Washington may increasingly shift pressure outward toward foreign entities sustaining Havana’s economic resilience.

Key indicators:

• Action against financial intermediaries
• Increased scrutiny of shipping and energy networks
• Pressure on foreign companies operating in sanctioned sectors
• Additional designations involving military-commercial structures

Objective: raise the external cost of sustaining Havana.

Indicators of movement would include:

• Senior-level diplomatic contacts

Selective sanctions relief could become bargaining leverage if Havana offers verifiable concessions.

Absent concessions, further economic isolation becomes increasingly plausible.

Three trajectories emerge:

A — NEGOTIATED ACCOMMODATION

Limited Cuban concessions produce selective U.S. relief.

B — PROLONGED COERCION

Havana absorbs the pressure while Washington continues constricting revenue and external support.

C — INTERNAL DESTABILIZATION

Economic deterioration, energy shortages, and declining state capacity generate larger protests or fractures within the governing structure.

STRATEGIC ASSESSMENT

The emerging U.S. model is cumulative:

CONSTRICT REVENUE
→ RESTRICT EXTERNAL SUPPORT
→ INCREASE INTERNAL ECONOMIC PRESSURE
→ PRESERVE NEGOTIATING LEVERAGE

This does not establish that Washington has decided on direct regime-change intervention.

Current public evidence is more consistent with coercive economic leverage, strategic isolation, and pressure designed to alter Havana’s decision calculus.

INDICATORS & WARNINGS

Watch closely for:

• Sanctions against third-country facilitators
• Action affecting Cuba’s fuel supply
• Unannounced senior U.S.–Cuba contacts
• Emergency Russian or Chinese assistance

DECISION WINDOW

The central intelligence question is no longer whether Washington intends to pressure Havana.

It is whether sustained pressure forces negotiation, drives Cuba toward deeper external dependence, or accelerates internal instability faster than the Cuban state can adapt.

text:
GRACO $GGG LEADS THE DEEP-VALUE LEN5. THE BUSINESS EARNS THE SEAT; THE PRICE DOES NOT YET:

Graco (GGG) at $78.37, +$0.73 / +0.94% on Wednesday, is the first of 113 names the Deep-Value & Special-Situations Len5 is watching. The 100-year-old Minneapolis company makes pumps, paint sprayers and dispensers for everything from wall paint to factory sealants. On August 31 it paid $447M in cash for Valco Melton, a maker of glue-dispensing machines; on Wednesday the 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.11%, up about 0.15 point.

The verdict: Graco is the kind of business this Len5 waits for - wide margins, almost no debt - but it is not priced below what it steadily earns. At 24.6 times its past year's profit, the discount half is missing, and the cash that padded the case is mostly spent. A watch, not a bargain.

Where the cash went:

- March 27: $712.2M on hand
- Three months to June 26: $315M to buy back about 4.0M of its own shares, near $78.50 each - roughly tonight's price
- August 31: $447M for Valco Melton, out of the $507.6M left on June 26

Valco Melton, based near Cincinnati, sells machines that lay glue on packaging lines and cameras that check the work: about $145M of 2025 sales, roughly 6.5% of Graco's. Net of expected tax savings, Graco puts the price at about 14 times Valco Melton's 2025 EBITDA, a rough cash-profit measure before interest, taxes and write-offs.

It buys into a slow market. Nordson (NDSN) at $321.42, +$1.75 / +0.55% on Wednesday, the larger rival, grew its adhesive-dispensing and coating segment 3% without acquisitions in the July quarter. Nordson fits none of the six Len5es; at about 32 times its past year's profit it offers none of the discount the value Len5es want.

The June quarter, reported July 22:

- Sales $590.6M, +3%, all from acquisitions and currency; without them, -1%
- Operating profit - what is left after making and selling the products - $175.1M, +11%; $9M came from refunds of tariffs the Supreme Court struck down in February, about half the $17.6M gain
- Orders without acquisitions up at a mid-single-digit rate

The strongest fact against the verdict is the Contractor segment, about half of sales. It sells sprayers to professional painters and home centers, and in June it grew in the Americas in both channels without help from deals for the first time in two years, CEO Mark Sheahan said. If orders keep climbing, profit can grow into the price. Rates cut the other way: painting and remodeling slow when borrowing costs climb, and Graco's profit comes to 4.1% of its price against 5.11% on a Treasury.

Graco through the six Len5es, plus the Quality Len5:

- DEEP-VALUE & SPECIAL-SITUATIONS - PARTIAL, and the Len5 watching it. Hunts a sound business priced below what it steadily earns. Sound: 21 cents of profit over four quarters per dollar of shareholders' equity - the owners' stake - and $29.2M of debt in June. Priced below: no. $12.7B of stock-market value is about 26 times its five-year average profit of $483M. What would knock Graco off the Deep-Value Len5: another deal paid for with borrowed money. What would make it a full fit: a price that falls while that profit holds.

- QUALITY-VALUE - PARTIAL, 28th of 63. Hunts a business almost nobody could rebuild, bought below its worth. The rebuild half: Graco kept 53.7 cents of each June-quarter sales dollar after the cost of making its products, and 29.6 cents after all operating costs. The price half fails as above. What would knock Graco off the Quality-Value Len5: that margin slipping once the tariff refunds stop.

- QUALITY LEN5 - FIT. Wants real gross profit, a solid return on the owners' stake, and debt no bigger than that stake: $316.9M of June-quarter gross profit; $533.5M of profit over four quarters on $2.52B of equity; debt about 1% of it. What would knock Graco off the Quality Len5: returns sliding as it pays up for more deals like Valco Melton.

- GROWTH - NOT A FIT. Hunts profit growth the price has not charged for, on a long profitable record. The record is there; the growth is not: sales $2.14B in 2022, $2.24B in 2025, and a 2026 plan for low single-digit growth without acquisitions. What would put Graco on the Growth Len5: growth without deals back to mid-single digits for several quarters.

- INCOME - NOT A FIT. Hunts cash to owners the business itself pays for. First-half free cash flow - cash left after running the business and buying equipment - was $269.5M against $97.7M of dividends, but the $1.18 yearly dividend yields 1.5%, and dividends plus $331.1M of buybacks outran that cash. What would put Graco on the Income Len5: a dividend that matters at this price, paid from cash flow.

- MOMENTUM - NOT A FIT. Hunts a price near its one-year high with short and long climbs agreeing. Graco is 18% under February's $95.69 high and 7.8% below a year ago. What would put Graco on the Momentum Len5: a climb back toward that high.

- HYPERGROWTH - NOT A FIT, the widest miss. Hunts very fast growth on a real base; Graco's sales grew about 4% in three years. What would put Graco on the Hypergrowth Len5: sales doubling in a few years, not how a century-old equipment maker grows.

WHEN: third-quarter results, tentatively October 21 after the close, not yet confirmed by Graco; analysts expect $0.83 a share. Graco guided sales of $580M-$600M before Valco Melton, vs $543.4M a year ago. The number that decides it: sales growth without acquisitions, after June's -1%. RISK: slower painting and remodeling under higher rates, just as the cash is gone.

Between late March and August 31, Graco put $762M behind two prices it judged fair: its own stock near $78.50, and Valco Melton at about 14 times its cash profit. The Deep-Value Len5 is still waiting for the market to offer a lower one.

Not investment advice.
